about.title: Livermore Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Public records list five traffic deaths in Livermore for 2025. Behind each of those counts is a household in Alameda County trying to figure out what comes next. Many of these crashes happen along I-580 in both directions and on Isabel Avenue, and the records show reported collisions cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters are heading home. A wrongful death claim is not about revenge. It is a civil case, separate from anything the district attorney may pursue, that asks the responsible party to account for what your family lost: funeral and burial expenses, the income and support your loved one would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance that cannot be replaced. California law limits who may bring the claim and gives most families two years from the date of death to act, with a shorter window when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service. We listen, then connect you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases in Livermore on a contingency basis.

whyChoose.title: Why Livermore Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are matched with can sort out who in your family has the right to bring the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the clock is much shorter when a city, county or state agency may share fault. Connecting sooner keeps those options open.

items.title: A civil path, apart from any criminal case
items.desc: Whether or not prosecutors bring charges, your family may pursue funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance through a separate civil action. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My relative was killed in a crash on I-580 near Livermore. Does the freeway location change anything?
items.answer: It can. Freeway collisions sometimes raise questions about road design, signage or maintenance, which may involve Caltrans or another public entity. Claims against government agencies in California carry a much shorter filing window than the standard two years, so it is wise to speak with an attorney quickly. The attorney can also gather CHP reports and other records specific to the I-580 corridor.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children. If there are none, certain other heirs or people who were financially dependent on the person who died may qualify. An attorney can review your family's situation and explain who has standing before any paperwork is filed.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter and runs on its own track, separate from any prosecution in Alameda County Superior Court. Your family does not need a conviction to move forward, and waiting could put the two-year deadline at risk. Many attorneys begin gathering evidence while the criminal case is still pending.
